title: Why are games still platform specific with AI?
author: mathaic
selftext:
So long story short I had an expensive gaming PC from my studies in AI that broke about 1 year ago and I have since not been able to afford to buy a new one due to high prices or RAM. At university for matlab work I used to use a Mac mini m1 as it just worked way faster it had been sitting in a box since about 2020 though. So now for the past year I have switched up and I am developing games on a Mac, initially it was very difficult especially without access to modern graphics APIs and such as someone who makes there own engines. In many languages though you have rendering libraries that are graphics API agnostic.

But anyway this is the thing I don’t get, why do people still only release games on windows? For example I can write a game in c or c++ then I asked AI how do I compile too other platforms wirhout access to such systems the main answers usually are to use the appropriate headers for that system eg mingw on mac for windows, but then in modern languages like Nim, rust, zig and such you can do it a lot easier in them.

This ain’t a rant just generally wondering why people with so much access to knowledge and tooling now still only release games on windows when publishing to other platforms is more straight forward than ever.

Even in popular game engines it’s very straight forward to do this.

comments.author: gamedevjp
comments.body: There’s a lot more to consider besides just “make it work here”. Lots of nuances. OS is a bit easier, but for Mac you need to have a developer license and have to keep it renewed if you want your game on any Apple Store. For consoles, each platform has their own process to get your game on. For example, you need to be a registered company like an LLC (which is about $800 / year in California) just to be able to apply for a partnership. Once approved you have to get their SDK since it’s not public, and then develop on that. A lot of barriers and associated recurring costs, so it’s not as simple to just write the code in a lower level language.

replies.author: mathaic
replies.body: Yeah consoles I 100% agree on as an indie dev I look at consoles as an eventual thing over time. But the Apple Store thing is a myth you can still package the binary in an app file and run it locally, distributing through other platforms like steam and itch and such. I admit on Mac it’s like they make it as awkward as possible and it’s not straight forward but that brings me back to my point with AI you can work it now so why not?

replies.author: gamedevjp
replies.body: You totally can do it on Mac. I think it’s really the associated costs and extra steps. Also, the knowledge of how to do it I think it might intimidate some? I find it easy because I make single player games so all of my games go on Mac. The only thing I have to consider is how to save files and resolution since I’m doing 2D

replies.author: gamedevjp
replies.body: I think another thing is most developers think no one plays on Mac when that’s absolutely not true

comments.author: DoSomeStrangeThings
comments.body:
Because maintaining a software over multiple platforms is more complex task than just releasing it to multiple platform. Web, Windows, Consoles and mobile all need different control schemes, support for totally different screen resolutions, regulations. Every time somethung is updated on one of them you need to go and ensure that your app still works. And fix if it doesn't which potentially break something on other platforms. 

Also going forward you need to develop with all of them in mind.

So yeah, releasing something half assed in all platforms is easy, maintaining it all is not, even with all the tools. 

Also in terms of gamedev. C++ is still king, and it is pain to make it work not in platform it was written for

replies.author: mathaic
replies.body:
I don’t code in C++ mainly and I disagree with that statement it may be used in a lot of companies but you can use any language really.

I feel like my point is getting missed on this post entirely. 

You mention maintaining I would normally agree but with AI doing that is way easier than before so I don’t think that’s a good reason anymore.

replies.author: DoSomeStrangeThings
replies.body:
You can write in assembly, but most of us don't. You can write all libraries yourself, but most us don't. 

Yes, AI increase development speed, but it is not a magic pill. You can work x2-x5-x20 times faster, but things still cost time and money. Even more so if you are not just vibe coding. 

So at some point you are supposed to ask yourself is it worth it to spend time and money to maintain a larger more complex code base written by mostly AI and not benefitting from libraries and frameworks available in more "established languages" to achieve... what?

replies.author: thatguywithimpact
replies.body:
With AI development is faster let's just throw a figure of 10-20x. But it's not magic, you still have to control a lot of things because AI is still bad at long term planning and his vision for the game sucks. You still gotta push through for weeks or even months of development.

But making multiplatform thing is just the easiest thing in the world - you basically say "make me an "android version of my game " and then maybe there's just a day or two UI specific refinement and it's done.

Because it's not about making game anymore it's just a software engineering problem, and this is almost entirely automated already.

comments.author: Sufficient_Gap_3029
comments.body: Windows is easier to develop for, more common and a huge percentage of the customer base.

replies.author: mathaic
replies.body: True but my point still stands that to cross compile can take a few mins and extend reach of your game making more money so why not take a few secs with AI to work it out?

replies.author: Lonely-Highlight-566
replies.body: You need to test your game on each platform.

replies.author: mathaic
replies.body: Testing can now be done by AI a lot faster

replies.author: Lonely-Highlight-566
replies.body: Not exactly. Having thousands of players means you’re going to have a lot of bugs and crashes. It could be a platform specific bug, or a general one. You will need to test it many times, the number of potential causes for the bug will increase.With every update, you’ll need to check across every platform to see if it’s still working.

comments.author: dark0mania
comments.body:
Because Apple devices are intentionally unfriendly and locked down in terms of development. Who would want to develop for someone who doesn't want you? 

With DirectX you can target Windows and Xbox
With Vulkan you can target Windows, Xbox and Playstation 
With Metal you can only target Apple devices.
